data.title: GATA Internal Controls Questionnaire (ICQ)
data.body_md:
> 📄 **Source:** NPSA internal Illinois NSGP ICQ Summary

The ICQ is one of the most important — and most overlooked — requirements for Illinois grants. It is a **pre-award hard gate** under GATA, not a post-award formality.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "GATA Internal Controls Questionnaire (ICQ)" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: What the ICQ Is
data.body_md:
- A **Fiscal & Administrative Risk Assessment** required by GATA
- Applies at the **organization level**, not per grant — one ICQ covers all Illinois grants for that org
- Must be **updated annually**
- Used to assign a **risk score** to the organization, which determines any special conditions attached to the grant agreement

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "What the ICQ Is" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: When It's Required
data.body_md:
| Stage | ICQ Status |
|-------|------------|
| Before application | Expected / often required |
| During application review | **Required — Illinois will not process the application without it** |
| Before grant award | **Mandatory** |

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "When It's Required" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: The Bottom Line
data.body_md:
> Illinois **will not approve or process an application** without a completed ICQ. An organization can submit a strong application and be selected by IEMA — and still not receive the award if the ICQ isn't done.

The ICQ is **not a post-award step.** It must be completed early in the process and directly affects eligibility, application approval, and the final grant agreement terms.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "The Bottom Line" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Practical Guidance
data.body_md:
- **Start the ICQ at the same time as GATA portal registration** — do not wait until closer to the application deadline.
- **First-time Illinois applicants:** Budget 4–6 weeks for full GATA setup including ICQ. This is not an exaggeration.
- **Returning applicants:** Verify the ICQ is current (updated within the past year) before each cycle. An expired ICQ causes the same delays as a missing one.
- The ICQ's risk score may result in additional reporting or compliance conditions being attached to the award — review any special conditions before signing the grant agreement.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Practical Guidance" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Timeline & Deadlines
data.body_md:
- **State Application Open Date:** Typically 2–4 weeks after FEMA NOFO release; IEMA publishes its own Notice of Funding on the GATA portal
- **State Application Deadline:** IEMA sets its own deadline — historically 30–45 days after state competition opens. **Verify with IEMA each cycle.**
- **SAA Review Period:** IEMA review typically takes 6–10 weeks.
- **Award Notification Timeline:** Subrecipients notified after FEMA awards IEMA; often late summer/fall.
- **Notes:** Like Texas, the IEMA state deadline is the binding deadline for subrecipients — not the FEMA deadline. GATA prequalification must be complete before an award can be made (even if the application was submitted).

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Timeline & Deadlines" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Eligibility Nuances
data.body_md:
- **State-Level Entity Restrictions:** Illinois follows FEMA baseline eligibility. No confirmed state-added restrictions, but verify with IEMA.
- **Faith-Based Organization Notes:** Faith-based orgs are common and well-supported applicants in Illinois, particularly in the Chicago metro. No known state-level restrictions.
- **School-Specific Notes:** Private/parochial schools are eligible under FEMA rules. Public schools generally not eligible. Jewish day schools and Catholic schools are common applicants in the Chicago area.
- **Other Eligible Entity Notes:** Jewish community organizations (JCCs, federations) are well-represented in Illinois NSGP applications.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Eligibility Nuances" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: State-Specific Supplemental Requirements
data.body_md:
Verify this list with IEMA each cycle — requirements can change:

- [ ] GATA Grantee Portal prequalification (must be complete before award — begin immediately)
- [ ] **Internal Controls Questionnaire (ICQ)** — required before application review and before award; applies org-wide; must be current (updated annually)
- [ ] Active SAM.gov / UEI registration
- [ ] IEMA-specific application forms (available through the state's designated submission portal)
- [ ] Programmatic Risk Assessment (GATA requirement for new grantees)
- [ ] Financial Risk Assessment (GATA — for new or high-risk grantees)
- [ ] Certificate of Incorporation / IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
- [ ] Physical security assessment or vulnerability assessment documentation
- [ ] Uniform Grant Agreement (UGA) compliance documentation (Illinois state requirement)

**Notes on supplemental forms:** Illinois's GATA framework adds more administrative overhead than most states. First-time applicants in Illinois should be warned to expect a longer onboarding process even after award. NPSA should factor GATA compliance support into scope for Illinois clients.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "State-Specific Supplemental Requirements" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Historical Notes & Patterns
data.body_md:
- **Chicago concentration:** The majority of Illinois NSGP awards historically go to Chicago-area organizations. Faith-based orgs (particularly Jewish and Catholic institutions) and Jewish community organizations are frequent recipients.
- **GATA learning curve:** Organizations new to Illinois grants often underestimate the GATA prequalification burden. Plan for 4–6 weeks of GATA setup for first-time applicants.
- **IEMA communication style:** IEMA has historically been less proactive in communicating updates to applicants than some other state SAAs. Recommend proactive outreach rather than waiting for notices.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Historical Notes & Patterns" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: The ICQ is a hard gate — not a formality
data.body_md: **The ICQ is a hard gate — not a formality.** Illinois will not process an application or issue an award without a completed Internal Controls Questionnaire (ICQ). This is separate from the GATA portal registration itself. An org can be registered in GATA, submit an application, even be selected — and still be blocked from receiving the award if the ICQ is missing or expired. Start it at the same time as portal registration. See the ICQ section above for full detail.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: The ICQ must be updated annually
data.body_md: **The ICQ must be updated annually.** Returning applicants who completed it in a prior cycle are not automatically current. Verify it's been refreshed within the past year before each new cycle begins.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: The state deadline is the real deadline
data.body_md: **The state deadline is the real deadline.** Same as Texas — IEMA's deadline for subrecipient applications is earlier than FEMA's. Missing IEMA's deadline ends the process.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Illinois has more administrative overhead than most states
data.body_md: **Illinois has more administrative overhead than most states.** Between GATA requirements, the Uniform Grant Agreement, and IEMA's own forms, Illinois applications are more complex to manage post-award than in many other states. Scope NPSA engagements accordingly.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Chicago UA is competitive
data.body_md: **Chicago UA is competitive.** The Chicago Urban Area receives significant NSGP-UA funding, but it also has a large pool of eligible applicants. A strong narrative and documented security assessment are especially important.

extra.prose_source: IL.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified April 2026 — FY 2025 cycle)

data.title: Contacts and portals shift
data.body_md: **Contacts and portals shift.** Illinois has changed its grant submission systems in recent cycles. Always verify the current portal at the start of a new cycle — do not assume last year's process applies.

data.title: Eligibility Nuances
data.body_md:
- **Federal Baseline:** 501(c)(3) status (described under §501(c)(3) IRC and tax-exempt under §501(a)); applicant must demonstrate high risk of terrorist or other extremist attack via the IJ.
- **NC-Added Restrictions:** None observed beyond federal baseline. NCEM has not published state-level eligibility additions.
- **Faith-Based Organization Notes:** Houses of worship are explicitly named in NCDPS's scoring guidance. Per NCDPS, sub-applicants self-certify as "ideology-based/spiritual/religious entities (Houses of Worship, Educational Institutions, Medical Facilities, etc.)" in their IJ for the FEMA 3× scoring factor. Verification by NCEM and FEMA.
- **School-Specific Notes:** Private/parochial schools eligible under federal rules. Schools that self-certify as ideology-based educational institutions receive the 3× scoring factor; secular educational institutions receive 2×.
- **Other Eligible Entity Notes:** Medical facilities and other nonprofits follow standard federal rules. Note NCDPS warns sub-applicants to **not include foreign nationals or noncitizens** in their leadership/board submission without proper vetting — and to be prepared to disclose whether the organization's mission involves supporting immigrants (FEMA uses the term "aliens") and whether it has DEI practices.

data.title: State-Specific Supplemental Requirements
data.body_md:
Required by NCEM in addition to the federal application package. All uploaded to Salesforce:

**Application stage (with the IJ submission):**

- [ ] **Investment Justification (IJ)** — federal form, downloaded from FEMA/NCDPS, completed in Adobe Acrobat (NOT browser). One IJ per site.
- [ ] **Vulnerability Assessment** — one per site. No NC-specific template — CISA Houses of Worship Self-Assessment (https://www.cisa.gov/publication/houses-worship-security-self-assessment) is accepted.
- [ ] **Mission Statement** — required; covers organization's purpose, values, and population served.
- [ ] **Supporting documentation** — police reports, photographs, threat evidence (if applicable). Include a brief description in the IJ.
- [ ] **Short bios + resumes of organizational leadership and board members** — names and business addresses only; **NO personal addresses, phone numbers, or other PII**. Uploaded with the application in Salesforce.
- [ ] **Self-certification of organization type** in the IJ — ideology-based/spiritual/religious, secular medical/educational, or other nonprofit. Determines the FEMA scoring multiplier.
- [ ] **501(c)(3) determination letter** — recommended for evidentiary support.
- [ ] **SAM.gov UEI** — not required at application, but **required before subaward**. Begin SAM.gov registration immediately.

**Post-award compliance documents** (uploaded to Salesforce after award; required to receive reimbursements):

- [ ] **NC Substitute W-9** (download from https://www.ncosc.gov/state-suppliers) — emailed to NCEMGrants1@ncdps.gov and cc'd to assigned grants manager, plus uploaded to Salesforce
- [ ] **Supplier Electronic Payment Form** (from same NC OSC page) — submit to NC OSC and upload to Salesforce. List Agency Name "NCDPS," Agency Contact "NCDPS Controller's Office," DOC.Controller@ncdps.gov, 919-716-3300
- [ ] **Certification of No Overdue Tax Debt** — download, complete, **sign and notarize**, then upload. Organizations with overdue tax debt under G.S. §105-243.1 are ineligible for payments/reimbursements
- [ ] **Conflict of Interest Policy** — must address conflicts involving management employees, board members, and other governing body members (per G.S. §143C-6-23)
- [ ] **Procurement Policy** — must adequately address purchasing under federal awards (FEMA Resource Library: Purchasing Under a FEMA Award is a good reference)

**Reimbursement-stage requirements:**

- [ ] **Summary of Invoices form** (https://www.ncdps.gov/media/13937/open) — submitted with every Request for Reimbursement (RFR), plus actual invoices and proof of payment
- [ ] **Annual Progress Report** (https://www.ncdps.gov/media/13935/open) — required each state FY (7/1–6/30) during the period of performance until grant closeout. **Grantees cannot be reimbursed if any annual report is overdue.**
- [ ] **EHP (Environmental & Historic Preservation) Screening Form** — required for any project that could affect environment or historic property (including fencing, cameras, ground-disturbing work). Submit via Salesforce; NCEM forwards to FEMA. **Work cannot begin until EHP approval is received** — starting early can disqualify the expenditure.
- [ ] **Pro-Rated Services Calculator** (https://www.ncdps.gov/pro-rated-grants/open) — required with reimbursement requests if the project includes service contracts or SaaS subscriptions; NCEM only reimburses the portion of the service utilized within the Period of Performance.

**Notes on supplemental forms:** All forms are downloadable from https://www.ncdps.gov/NCEMGrants. The SOG (https://public.powerdms.com/DPSNC/tree) contains step-by-step walkthroughs for every post-award process.

data.title: Scoring (NCEM Process)
data.body_md:
NCEM scores applications using the federal NSGP Scoring Criteria published in Appendix D of the NOFO. NCDPS hosts the standalone scoring criteria document at https://www.ncdps.gov/media/14461/open.

**NCEM's scoring workflow:**
1. Verify eligibility and confirm location is inside (NSGP-UA) or outside (NSGP-S) the Charlotte UASI.
2. Score complete application packages (IJ + vulnerability assessment + mission statement) against the federal scoring criteria.
3. Validate the self-certified organization type by comparing the mission statement against the central purpose described.
4. Rank every IJ uniquely (#1 = highest through the total number of applications scored).

**FEMA's downstream multiplier (applied to the NCEM score):**
- **3×** — ideology-based/spiritual/religious entities (HoW, religious schools, religious medical facilities)
- **2×** — secular medical and educational institutions
- **1×** — all other nonprofits
- **+15 points** — first-time applicants (never received an NSGP award)

**Disqualifying defects:** Using a prior-year IJ form, submitting a scanned copy of the IJ, or leaving any required field blank → IJ deemed incomplete. No substitutes accepted for the current-year IJ form.

data.title: Historical Notes & Patterns
data.body_md:
- **NC consistently ranks among the top 4 NSGP-S states** by allocation. FY23 ≈ $4.9M, FY24 ≈ $4.3M, FY25 ≈ $3.95M. Even in a year of national contraction, NC remains an outsized opportunity.
- **NCEM takes 5% state M&A** off the top of both NSGP-S and NSGP-UA allocations (visible in FY23 figures: $245,810 of $4,916,198 NSGP-S; $61,481 of $1,229,611 Charlotte UA). This reduces dollars available to subrecipients but is the standard federal allowance and is not an NC quirk.
- **Application window has been compressed:** FY24 was ~45 days (4/16 NOFO → 5/31 deadline). FY25 was ~14 weeks from NOFO (7/28) to deadline (11/7), but the Salesforce window itself was only 37 days. Treat the post-NOFO window as 30–45 days regardless of when the NOFO drops.
- **FY24 → FY25 "different projects" guidance:** NCDPS publicly recommended that applicants who got FY24 NSGP-NSS funding or were denied FY24 NSGP **apply for different projects in FY25**. NCEM intended to use FY24 NSGP-NSS dollars to backfill some unfunded FY24 NSGP applications. Worth checking client history before drafting the FY26 IJ.
- **NCEM is well-organized but communicates almost entirely via the NCDPS website + Salesforce.** Unlike Washington (proactive email blasts) or Utah (named point of contact), NC's communication is web-first. Monitor https://www.ncdps.gov/NSGP regularly during NOFO season.

data.title: Salesforce registration is gated and reviewed
data.body_md: **Salesforce registration is gated and reviewed.** Each board member or staff representative needs their own user ID. Up to 5 active contacts per org. Submitting fraudulent registrations is a criminal offense in NC (up to 5 years per violation per NCDPS). Plan for a 1–2 business day approval cycle before users can access the org's account. **Start the Salesforce registration the day the engagement opens** — not the week of the deadline.

data.title: Consultants representing multiple NC orgs need a unique email per org in Salesforce
data.body_md: **Consultants representing multiple NC orgs need a unique email per org in Salesforce.** Same email across orgs will be denied. Use plus-addressing (e.g., stuart+orgA@npsa.com, stuart+orgB@npsa.com) or distinct aliases if working with multiple NC clients in one cycle.

data.title: Bios and resumes: business addresses only, no personal PII
data.body_md: **Bios and resumes: business addresses only, no personal PII.** NCEM forwards leadership info to DHS Office of Intelligence & Analysis for a post-selection security review. Clients sometimes send full personal contact info — scrub it before upload.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: Self-certification of organization type matters more than people realize
data.body_md: **Self-certification of organization type matters more than people realize.** A house of worship that mis-certifies as "other nonprofit" loses the 3× FEMA multiplier — that's the difference between a competitive and uncompetitive application. NCEM cross-checks the self-certification against the mission statement; the mission statement must clearly substantiate the certification.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: First-time applicants get +15 points from FEMA
data.body_md: **First-time applicants get +15 points from FEMA.** Worth a sentence in client kickoff — if this is the org's first NSGP attempt, lean into that scoring boost; if they've been denied before, the +15 doesn't apply but the FY25 "different project" pattern matters.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: No state-funded supplemental program
data.body_md: **No state-funded supplemental program.** NC has not authorized a state-level nonprofit security grant program. The federal NSGP is the only path. Re-verify annually — there has been advocacy from NC's congressional delegation (Rep. Ross, Gov. Cooper) for additional federal funding, but no NC-specific appropriation has surfaced.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: EHP screening is a real timing risk
data.body_md: **EHP screening is a real timing risk.** Outdoor projects (fencing, cameras on exterior walls, ground-penetrating installations) need EHP approval **before work begins**. Clients who start their fencing project in March and submit an EHP form in April will not be reimbursed. Build EHP screening into the immediate post-award workflow.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: Annual report compliance blocks reimbursement
data.body_md: **Annual report compliance blocks reimbursement.** If a client falls behind on the 7/1–6/30 annual progress report, NCEM will not process RFRs until they're current. Set calendar reminders for any awarded NC client.

extra.prose_source: NC.md, "Gotchas & Non-Obvious Notes" (last verified May 13, 2026 — FY25 cycle closed, FY26 pre-NOFO)

data.title: Post-award compliance docs are non-trivial
data.body_md: **Post-award compliance docs are non-trivial.** Notarized Tax Debt Certification, W-9, electronic payment setup with OSC, conflict-of-interest policy, procurement policy — clients without nonprofit grant management experience often don't have these ready. Flag them at kickoff so they can build/locate them in parallel with the IJ.

data.title: The Charlotte UASI is small
data.body_md: **The Charlotte UASI is small.** Only 8 counties. The vast majority of NC nonprofits — including all of Raleigh-Durham, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, Asheville, Wilmington, the Outer Banks — are NSGP-S. Don't over-index on Charlotte unless a client has a Charlotte-metro site.

data.title: State-Funded Supplemental Programs
data.body_md:
**No state-funded supplemental programs identified — verify annually.**

As of May 2026, NC operates only the federal NSGP. There is no NC analogue to NY SCAHC, FL-NSGP, CA CSNSGP, or PA NSGFP. NC's congressional delegation (Rep. Deborah Ross, Sen. Tillis) and former Gov. data.title: Timeline & Deadlines — TEXAS RUNS TWO STAGES
data.body_md:
⚠️ **Texas splits the application into two deadlines, and the first one lands months before the
federal NOFO exists.** This is the single most important thing on this page.

**STAGE 1 — eGrants application CREATED, SUBMITTED and CERTIFIED.**
FY2026: the system opened **1/12/2026**; certification closed **3/12/2026 at 5:00 PM CT**.

**STAGE 2 — documents uploaded to the Upload.Files tab**, roughly 10 days after the federal NOFO.
FY2026: **7/6/2026 at 5:00 PM CT**.

- **Deadline authority:** state. PSO's deadlines bind and land earlier than FEMA's SAA deadline.
- **No extensions**, and a submission **cannot be corrected** after the deadline closes.
- **Award notices:** roughly within 45 days of the federal award to Texas.

data.title: Eligibility Nuances
data.body_md:
- **Federal Baseline:** Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (or described under 501(c)(3) of IRC and tax-exempt under section 501(a)); must demonstrate high risk of terrorist or other extremist attack.
- **Washington State-Added Requirement:** Applicants **must complete a Notice of Intent (NOI) form** to have their application considered for funding. This is explicitly noted in WA EMD's communication as an *additional Washington state requirement* beyond FEMA's baseline.
- **Faith-Based Organization Notes:** Houses of worship explicitly referenced in WA EMD's vulnerability assessment guidance (CISA Houses of Worship Security Self-Assessment cited as an option).
- **School-Specific Notes:** Private/parochial schools eligible under federal rules. Public schools generally not eligible. Verify any state-level guidance with WA EMD.
- **Other Eligible Entity Notes:** Standard FEMA eligibility applies; confirm with WA EMD for any further state-level restrictions.

data.title: State-Specific Supplemental Requirements
data.body_md:
Washington has confirmed additional requirements beyond the standard FEMA application package:

- [ ] **Notice of Intent (NOI)** — *Washington state requirement* — Must be submitted by **May 31, 2026** via Microsoft Forms (link on NSGP Applicant website). Required to have application considered.
- [ ] **Vulnerability Assessment** — Must be current (within the last 3 years). Options:
  - Local law enforcement in-person assessment, OR
  - CISA Houses of Worship Security Self-Assessment (https://www.cisa.gov/houses-worship-security-self-assessment)
- [ ] **Investment Justification (IJ) form** — Must be completed in Adobe Acrobat (not browser). FY26 template not yet released; will be posted on NSGP Applicant website when available from FEMA.
- [ ] **Mission Statement** — Required; WA EMD prefers submission on organizational letterhead.
- [ ] **SAM.gov UEI** — Required before award. Begin immediately.
- [ ] 501(c)(3) determination letter / documentation of nonprofit status

**Notes on supplemental forms:** All forms downloadable from https://mil.wa.gov/grants-nsgp-application-details. WA EMD explicitly recommends drafting IJ narrative answers in Word first due to character limits in the Adobe form.

data.title: Historical Notes & Patterns
data.body_md:
- **FY26 cycle is early/active:** WA EMD communicated proactively in April 2026 ahead of NOFO release, indicating a well-organized SAA. The NOI deadline of May 31, 2026 is set while the NOFO is still pending — unusual and worth noting.
- **WA EMD offers technical assistance:** Open office hours with self-service scheduling are available. This is a resource to offer clients who have questions about the application.
- **First-cycle observation:** WA EMD's communication style is proactive and detailed, with explicit guidance on tools (Adobe Acrobat requirement, Word drafting recommendation) that other states don't provide. Suggests a thorough review process.

data.title: The NOI is a Washington gate, not a FEMA one
data.body_md: **The NOI is a Washington gate, not a FEMA one.** Clients in other states may not be used to a Notice of Intent requirement. In Washington, skipping the NOI (even with a great application) will disqualify the applicant. Submit by May 31, 2026 — even before the full application is ready.

data.title: The IJ form does not work in a browser
data.body_md: **The IJ form does not work in a browser.** Adobe Acrobat is required. This catches applicants off guard — especially faith-based orgs that may not have Adobe installed. Flag this early and have them install it before they try to open the form.
